originalFindings.claim: All six contextual tasks leave the particle inside the blank but omit ordinary topical は from acceptance. 窓は開いています, 窓は開けてあります, 窓は開けておきます and the corresponding 電気は forms preserve the respective requested meanings. The visible instructions do not limit particles to ga/wo or exclude a topic.
originalFindings.impact: Typed mode rejects familiar grammatical realizations of the tested answer class and suggests an unwarranted particle restriction. Existing fixed options and the two additional correct wo options are not themselves wrong.
originalFindings.remedy: Accept the fitting は realizations in all six tasks, preserving supported lexical spellings, and explain topical framing. Keep existing ga/wo options correct; any offered topical button must belong to the same accepted class. Do not invent a ga/wo-only restriction solely to narrow acceptance.

originalFindings.claim: Two te-iru formation tasks, two plain-state contextual tasks and two future-preparation tasks silently omit ordinary polite contractions, for example 開いてます, 消えてます, が開いてます, が消えてます, を開けときます and を消しときます. Kana and polite-nonpast requirements do not expressly require uncontracted or formal-business forms.
originalFindings.impact: Learners can preserve the supplied lexical verb, participant roles, stage, politeness and communicative goal yet be marked wrong. This is not a demand for separate contraction-discrimination practice.
originalFindings.remedy: Accept fitting polite contractions with supported lexical spellings and a conversational-register note. Only an actual full-form assembly operation should explicitly demand uncontracted forms; do not add such a restriction to contextual tasks merely to force one spelling. Preserve issue 20 ownership and existing SRS identities.

evidence.passage: Actual public-page polite_structure includes uncontracted おきます and contracted ときます; public preparation example accepts 調べておきます/調べときます.
Public lesson caution explicitly says contraction applies even to てます; result-state examples include contracted polite alternatives.
Conjugation section distinguishes polite endings and conversational contraction. Conversational register is not identical to plain-form grammar.

originalFindings.claim: The two noun-based becoming tasks also permit 会議室となりました and 公園となりました in their completed role-conversion scenes. These retain the displayed が phrase and ordinary polite-past なる predicate, but the answer lists permit only に. The visible instructions do not specifically demand に or exclude a formal/result-focused presentation.
originalFindings.impact: A broader noun-role-change operation is graded as an unstated に-only task, although the learner is not asked to discriminate に from と.
originalFindings.remedy: Accept the noun + となりました realizations and their kana spellings, with a short register/result-focus note. Keep the same become-change identity and N4 level. Do not automatically generalize to all na-adjectives, to-suru uses or arbitrary paraphrases.

evidence.passage: Noun sections include 雨は雪となった, role-change examples and written/formal/result-stage qualifications. Adjective attachment is treated separately.

originalFindings.claim: Four wrong-option te-oku rationales say the scene explicitly states the action has not happened yet. The arranged-state prompts explicitly state it has already been done; the plain-state prompts state only the present condition and unknown cause. The future-task explanation was copied into incompatible scenes.
originalFindings.impact: Answer feedback contradicts or invents the central stage evidence, confusing the difference between an option's proposed account and the actual scene.
originalFindings.remedy: Make these four rationales scene-specific. In arranged-result tasks explain the requested already-arranged result versus preparatory-action reporting; in plain-state tasks explain the unwanted preparation perspective without inventing an undone action. Keep not-yet language only where the prompt supplies it, and do not imply te-oku is universally future-only.
